stem_book: A block m₁ rests on the inclined face (angle θ) of a wedge m₂ that lies on a smooth horizontal table; the wedge is pulled by a light string passing over a smooth pulley at the table edge to a hanging mass m₃ (all surfaces smooth). The value of m₃ such that it is just able to prevent relative motion of m₁ with respect to m₂ is equal to (a) (m₁ + m₂)tanθ/(1 − tanθ) (b) (m₁ + m₂)cotθ/(1 − cotθ) (c) (m₁ + m₂)sinθ/(1 − sinθ) (d) (m₁ + m₂)cosθ/(1 − cosθ)
work: No slip needs a = g tanθ; m₃g = (m₁+m₂+m₃)a → m₃(1 − tanθ) = (m₁+m₂)tanθ
